scope: 0ef6970..4c3d9b0 is one commit, 4c3d9b0, touching ADOPTING.md, AGENT-USAGE.md, CHANGELOG.md, CLAUDE.md, EFFORT.md, README.md, bin/new-tool.mjs (fence only), package.json (0.4.1 -> 0.5.0), skeleton/tool.mjs (header and fence), skeleton/tool.test.mjs, test/new-tool.test.mjs. Nothing outside the brief.

settled.CLAUDE.md invariant 1: Human, --brief, --json and --quiet are all rendered by report() from the same items array.
settled.CLAUDE.md invariant 7: stdout is data, stderr is diagnostics. --json stdout is JSON only.
settled.CLAUDE.md invariant 10: Text modes escape control characters (printable() …) … so a filename can neither break a line, reorder it, nor trip the guard.
settled.CLAUDE.md invariant 12: The fence is byte-identical everywhere … A revision has no number of its own … 0.5.0 is the first … the sha256 moves from caf3bd4c… to 27679d92….
settled.CLAUDE.md invariant 13: Text output is frozen, except the --brief item line … and the human layout, which changed once … --brief is never longer than the human output of the same run.
settled.CLAUDE.md invariant 15: The default human mode and --help carry it; --brief, --quiet and --json never do, byte for byte … Escape first, then bold … a mark that is not a string, is blank or holds a control character (TAB included) is dropped whole.

suite.runs: piped 107/107; on a pty (script -q) 107/107; on a pty with TERM=dumb 107/107

byteIdentity.method: The 0ef6970 and 4c3d9b0 skeletons run in turn from one path with one package.json (so paths and version match): 20 argument sets (inspect/apply over ok, empty, directory, missing, protected and 11 hostile filenames: ESC/SGR, C1 CSI, RLO, U+2028, LF, TAB, a label-shaped name, emoji; --go, --yes, --note, usage errors, --version, --cheat) x 6 mode sets (human, --brief, --quiet, --json, --brief --quiet, --json --brief) x 7 environments (none, NO_COLOR=1, FORCE_COLOR=1, FORCE_COLOR=0, TERM=dumb, FORCE_COLOR=1+NO_COLOR=1, FORCE_COLOR=empty) x piped and pty; stdout, stderr and exit compared; Node’s own “(node:PID)” warning normalised.
byteIdentity.result: 1680 runs: 1470 non-human runs byte-identical (stdout, stderr, exit); 210 human runs identical once SGR 1/22 and blank lines are removed, with stderr and exit identical; 0 differ. Scaffolder: 44 runs (four modes, good/bad --author, bad name, unknown flag, unwritable --dir, --version, --cheat, plain and FORCE_COLOR): non-human identical except the byte counts of the larger template files in --json data; human equivalent.

injection: 1037 in-process checks over 23 hostile strings (ESC, SGR 1/22/0, OSC 8, C1 CSI, DECSET, DCS, RLO, LRI/PDI, U+2028/2029, label-shaped and summary/next-shaped text) placed in name, summary, lines, reason and mark, bold on and off: no live ESC or C1 outside the renderer’s own pairs, no raw LS/PS/bidi control, every line’s bold balanced (no SGR left open at a line end), one summary and one next: line; marks never in --brief/--quiet/--json. Labels: 33 positive/negative cases match the documented rule except F5. 1 MB strings render in 13-26 ms.
help: Every adopted header (81 files carrying the v3 fence) spliced into the old and new skeleton: same lines in the same order, only blank lines added, bold unbolds to the plain text, no escape byte piped. Real fence swap in scratch copies of adopted tool A (a key-file manager, private), adopted tool C, adopted tool D and adopted tool E: --help same lines and order, 7/4/1/0 blank lines added, exit 0, stderr unchanged.
adoption: ADOPTING 0.5.0 followed on a scratch copy of adopted tool A (a key-file manager, private): fence swapped (no name collision there), pin moved (F2), FORCE_COLOR/NO_COLOR deleted in the test file; 90/90 piped and on a pty; human list output reads with bold labels and a blank line between keys. adopted tool E copy after the swap: 47/48, only the fence pin red, piped and on a pty. adopted tool D copy after the swap: 49/49 piped; on a pty 46/49 (the unmodified copy is 47/49 there: --clock is red at a terminal already, and its live-skeleton fence test is red until it re-syncs); with step 4’s two delete lines it is 49/49 on a pty, so step 4 is needed and sufficient there. Scaffold of a new tool: fence 27679d92, its own suite 68/68 piped and on a pty.
forceColorUnderNodeTest: Confirmed: a test file run by node --test on a pty sees FORCE_COLOR="1" (also with --test-reporter=tap); piped, under NO_COLOR, or with TERM=dumb it is unset. Both repo test files delete FORCE_COLOR/NO_COLOR, and M47/M48 show those lines are load-bearing at a terminal.
sources: no-color.org, force-color.org and nodejs.org/api/cli.html read raw (curl) on 2026-11-06: NO_COLOR “present and not an empty string (regardless of its value)”; FORCE_COLOR “present and not an empty string (regardless of its value)” forces colour; Node: “1, true, or the empty string” enable, “When FORCE_COLOR is used and set to a supported value, both the NO_COLOR, and NODE_DISABLE_COLORS … are ignored. Any other value will result in colorized output being disabled.” The code comment and CHANGELOG describe the hybrid accurately.

fence: Block (markers included, no trailing newline) sha256 27679d92f2ce237031c20279286eaeffe9141668b7ea9ee0ecfcdb9aba612405 in skeleton/tool.mjs and bin/new-tool.mjs, byte-identical; 0ef6970 block caf3bd4cb6f99432ea87c80884c86ec6fec7023ad6ef06423aeda27f837b22df; with the trailing newline, 1f1c5c19… -> c4e528bb…. Marker runtime v3 and CONTRACT mjs-tool/3 unchanged; package 0.5.0. Top-level names added: boldEnabled, boldWith, LABEL_WORD, LABEL, boldLabels, MARK_MAX, markOf, HELP_HEADING, HELP_COMMAND; none dropped. All 81 adopted tool files still pin caf3bd4c.

findings.summary: The new fence declares a top-level `const LABEL`, and adopted tool B (a launchd alert script, private) already declares `const LABEL` above its fence (line 152), so swapping the 0.5.0 fence in as ADOPTING says makes tool B fail to load: SyntaxError, exit 1 (the one exit the runtime cannot turn into 3), on a launchd alerting tool. ADOPTING’s 0.5.0 step 1 says to search for the new names but neither it nor the builder’s report names this hit; 1 of the 81 adopted tool files scanned collides.
findings.location: skeleton/tool.mjs:771 and bin/new-tool.mjs:817 (const LABEL); ADOPTING.md:966-971 (0.5.0 step 1); adopted tool B:152
findings.repro: Copy adopted tool B to scratch, replace its fence with the 0.5.0 block, then `node --check copy.mjs` -> "SyntaxError: Identifier 'LABEL' has already been declared" at the fence’s `const LABEL = new RegExp(...)`, exit 1; `node copy.mjs --help` -> same, exit 1. A top-level name scan of the 81 adopted tool files for the nine new names finds only this one.
findings.acceptance: Either (preferred, while no tool has adopted 0.5.0: all 81 still pin caf3bd4c) the fence’s `LABEL`/`LABEL_WORD` take fence-specific names that no adopted tool declares (re-scan the fleet), with FENCE_SHA256, CLAUDE.md invariant 12, CHANGELOG and ADOPTING’s name list moved to the new hash; or ADOPTING’s 0.5.0 step 1 names tool B’s `LABEL` as a known collision to rename in that tool when it re-syncs. Either way, a scan of the adopted tools for the new names is part of the release record.
findings.likelihood: likely (certain for tool B when it re-syncs)
findings.cause: A generic top-level name in a block that is copied byte for byte into 81 files, and no fleet scan before release.

findings.summary: ADOPTING’s 0.5.0 step 2 gives only the no-trailing-newline sha256 (27679d92…), but most adopted fence tests pin the hash taken with the newline (1f1c5c19… for 0.4.x; 28 files found, against 10 on caf3bd4c…). Following step 2 literally leaves tool A’s fence test red; its 0.5.0 value is c4e528bb….
findings.repro: Scratch copy of adopted tool A (a key-file manager, private), fence swapped: set its pin (its test file:107, which hashes fence + "\n") to 27679d92f2ce237031c20279286eaeffe9141668b7ea9ee0ecfcdb9aba612405 -> 89/90, "the runtime fence is the skeleton fence, byte for byte" fails; with c4e528bbca359824786958256d51b84c7205d00df99e9cbe2a9410549234bf69 -> 90/90.
findings.acceptance: The 0.5.0 section names both values, 27679d92… (block alone) and c4e528bb… (block plus the newline after the closing marker), as §6 asks a pinned value to say which it covers.
findings.likelihood: likely (every adopter on the with-newline form)
findings.cause: The section quotes the skeleton’s own pin form only.

findings.summary: boldEnabled() ignores TERM=dumb: on a dumb terminal (TTY with TERM=dumb) the human mode and --help write SGR bytes, though the code comment and CHANGELOG promise bold “only where it will be read as bold”; Node itself reports hasColors() false there, and node --test does not force colour under TERM=dumb.
findings.location: skeleton/tool.mjs:753-757 (and the same lines in bin/new-tool.mjs)
findings.repro: TERM=dumb script -q /dev/null node skeleton/tool.mjs inspect report.txt < /dev/null | cat -v -> "^[[1mreport.txt^[[22m", "^[[1mkind:^[[22m file"; TERM=dumb script -q /dev/null node -e 'console.log(process.stdout.hasColors(), process.stdout.getColorDepth())' -> "false 1".
findings.acceptance: With no FORCE_COLOR, a TTY whose TERM is `dumb` gets no escape byte (human and --help), with a test row in the bold matrix; or the docs drop “only where it will be read as bold” and name TERM=dumb as a Known limit.
findings.cause: The gate reads NO_COLOR, FORCE_COLOR and isTTY only.

findings.summary: A mark with a control character at either end is trimmed and kept, not “dropped whole” as CLAUDE.md invariant 15, CHANGELOG, README and the code comment say: "🟢\n", "\t🟢" and "🟢\u2028" all print as 🟢 (String.prototype.trim runs before the control check). Nothing unsafe reaches the line.
findings.location: skeleton/tool.mjs:783-784 (markOf); CLAUDE.md:220-223; CHANGELOG.md:44-46; README.md:183-189; skeleton/tool.mjs:779-780 comment
findings.repro: report() in-process with items [{…, summary: "key: v", mark: "🟢\n"}] (likewise "\t🟢", "🟢\u2028") -> summary line "    🟢 key: v"; the docs say the mark is dropped, i.e. "    key: v".
findings.acceptance: Either the control check runs before trim (so those marks drop, with test rows for a leading TAB and a trailing LF/U+2028), or the docs say a mark is trimmed first and dropped when a control character remains inside it.
findings.cause: trim() removes TAB, LF, CR, VT, FF, U+2028 and U+2029 at the ends before CONTROL_CHARS is tested.

findings.summary: The docs say a sentence with a colon is never bolded, but any one-to-three-word lowercase phrase that opens a summary or a lines entry is: "the file was: gone" and "could not read: EACCES" bold the whole phrase.
findings.location: skeleton/tool.mjs:763-769 (comment: “a sentence with a colon in it is never bolded”); CHANGELOG.md:39-40 (“a sentence is never bolded”); README.md:175; CLAUDE.md:215
findings.repro: report() with lines ["the file was: gone"] under FORCE_COLOR -> "\x1b[1mthe file was:\x1b[22m gone".
findings.acceptance: The docs say what the rule is (a phrase of four or more words, or one with a capital or punctuation, is not a label), or the rule changes; the test’s negatives keep a three-word case either way.
findings.cause: Word count is the only sentence test.

notBlocking.summary: 32 of the 81 adopted tool headers wrap the “Output modes (all rendered from the same item objects, so they can never / disagree):” heading over two lines; after re-sync that heading prints plain under bold Usage:/Commands:/Flags:. Other shapes read unevenly too: adopted tool G’s “Commands (both read-only; …):” is bold but its entries are not spaced or bolded; adopted tool H’s “Options, search:” is plain; prose lead-ins such as adopted tool I’s “Each side is flagged when the certificate:” and tool A’s “Installing a key without it passing through a shell history:” are bold. Documented (“a header shaped otherwise prints as written”; ADOPTING §2), so this is adoption work, not a fence defect.
notBlocking.repro: Each adopted header spliced into the old and the new skeleton: 81/81 print the same lines in the same order with only blank lines added (143 in all) and unbold to the plain text; the bold set is listed per tool.
notBlocking.acceptance: ADOPTING’s 0.5.0 step 5 says to re-wrap a two-line heading onto one line (32 tools), and optionally HELP_COMMAND/inCommands accept a `Commands (…):` heading.

notBlocking.summary: The mark cap counts code points, so a mark of more than eight can be cut inside a ZWJ sequence, leaving a dangling U+200D: "🟢🟢👨‍👩‍👧‍👦" prints "🟢🟢👨‍👩‍👧‍". The test’s “a joined emoji sequence stays whole” holds only at eight or fewer.
notBlocking.repro: report() with mark "🟢🟢👨‍👩‍👧‍👦" (9 code points) -> code points 1f7e2,1f7e2,1f468,200d,1f469,200d,1f467,200d.
notBlocking.acceptance: Cut at a grapheme boundary (Intl.Segmenter) or say “code points, which can split a joined emoji” in the docs.

notBlocking.summary: The bidi marks U+200E, U+200F and U+061C (and other invisible format characters) pass printable() and the mark check, so a mark or a name can carry one; the scaffolder refuses the same marks in --author (R3-2). Pre-existing for names; the mark is a new place for it.
notBlocking.repro: report() with mark "\u200f🟢" -> summary line holds U+200F before the emoji.
notBlocking.acceptance: Either CONTROL_CHARS takes the three bidi marks (a fence change: decide with F1’s rename), or a Known limit says they pass.
